title: Interstate child support enforcement
facts: Federal and uniform state-law systems support enforcement of child-support orders when parents live in different states.
A parent generally does not need a new support obligation merely because the other parent moves to another state; jurisdiction and modification rules determine which tribunal controls the order.
State child-support agencies can work across state lines to locate parents, establish obligations and enforce qualifying orders.
International child-support enforcement can involve separate treaty or reciprocal-country procedures.
